# Custom CSS Themes

A theme changes the whole look of Marinara: colors, fonts, pictures and the shape of panels. Marinara has a gallery of ready-made starter themes you can download. You can also import a theme someone shared, or make your own.

For a quick change with no theme at all, see [Appearance Settings](appearance-settings.md) or [Ready-made chat window styles](#ready-made-chat-window-styles). To make your own theme, the [Theme Author Guide](theme-author-guide.md) walks you through it step by step.

## What a custom theme is

A theme is a block of CSS, the code web pages use for colors, fonts and spacing, plus any pictures and fonts it brings along. Themes are saved on your Marinara server, so a theme you install shows up on every device that connects to it. Only one theme is on at a time, and you can keep as many as you like.

## Where to find themes

Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections. In the classic layout it is **Settings → Addons → Theme Library**.

The section has:

- **Create Theme** and **Import File** at the top.
- **Allow themes with HTML (I accept the risk)**, off by default. See [Themes with HTML](#themes-with-html).
- **Installed Themes**: **Default Theme**, then your own themes, then the starter themes you downloaded.
- **Browse the theme gallery**: the starter themes you can download.

## Starter themes

Starter themes aren't part of the install, so they take no space until you want one. They live in the theme gallery, and Marinara downloads a theme only when you pick it.

1. Click **Browse the theme gallery** under **Installed Themes**. Marinara needs an internet connection for this.
2. Each theme shows a preview, a short description, its size and its tags.
3. Click **Download** next to the ones you like. They appear under **Starter themes** in **Installed Themes**, ready to switch on.

# Theme Author Guide

This guide is for people who make or share their own themes. The first part walks you through your first theme with no coding experience needed. The rest is a reference: every colour, picture and part a theme can change, and the safety rules every theme follows. To pick, try, import or remove a theme, see [Custom CSS Themes](custom-css-themes.md).

**Token contract version 1** (`--mari-tokens-version: 1` on `:root`). The names in this guide keep working between releases. When one has to change, the version goes up and the change is listed under [Changes](#changes) at the end. Everything else (other `--ov-*`, `--mari-*` and `--marinara-*` variables, Tailwind classes, element structure) is internal and can change in any update.

## Your first theme, step by step

A theme is a short list of settings written in CSS, the language web pages use for colours and fonts. You don't need to know CSS to start. Each line looks like `--name: value;`: a **token** (a named setting that starts with `--`), a colon, the value, and a semicolon.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections.
2. To change a starter theme, download one you like from **Browse the theme gallery**, find it under **Starter themes** and click **Clone + Edit** (the copy icon). Marinara makes your own copy, named for example "Petal OS (my copy)", and opens it in the editor. Starter themes stay read-only, so the original is always there. To start from scratch instead, click **Create Theme**. Its template has lines between `/*` and `*/`, which are switched off. Delete those marks around a line to switch it on.
3. Type a name in the name box.
4. Change a colour. Find a line such as `--primary: #3fae7a;` and replace the colour. `#3fae7a` is a hex colour code. Any colour picker on the web gives you one. Names such as `teal` work too.
5. Leave **Preview** on. The app changes as you type, so you see each change at once.
6. Look under the editor. **No CSS problems found.** means the CSS is fine. Otherwise each problem shows with its line number, such as a missing `;` or `}`.
7. Click **Save**. Your new theme turns on, and Marinara asks **Keep this theme?** Click **Keep theme** within 15 seconds, or it goes back to your old look.

# Theme Author Guide

This guide is for people who make or share their own themes. The first part walks you through your first theme with no coding experience needed. The rest is a reference: every colour, picture and part a theme can change, and the safety rules every theme follows. To pick, try, import or remove a theme, see [Custom CSS Themes](custom-css-themes.md).

**Token contract version 1** (`--mari-tokens-version: 1` on `:root`). The names in this guide keep working between releases. When one has to change, the version goes up and the change is listed under [Changes](#changes) at the end. Everything else (other `--ov-*`, `--mari-*` and `--marinara-*` variables, Tailwind classes, element structure) is internal and can change in any update.

## Your first theme, step by step

A theme is a short list of settings written in CSS, the language web pages use for colours and fonts. You don't need to know CSS to start. Each line looks like `--name: value;`: a **token** (a named setting that starts with `--`), a colon, the value, and a semicolon.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections.
2. To change a starter theme, download one you like from **Browse the theme gallery**, find it under **Starter themes** and click **Clone + Edit** (the copy icon). Marinara makes your own copy, named for example "Petal OS (my copy)", and opens it in the editor. Starter themes stay read-only, so the original is always there. To start from scratch instead, click **Create Theme**. Its template has lines between `/*` and `*/`, which are switched off. Delete those marks around a line to switch it on.
3. Type a name in the name box.
4. Change a colour. Find a line such as `--primary: #3fae7a;` and replace the colour. `#3fae7a` is a hex colour code. Any colour picker on the web gives you one. Names such as `teal` work too.
5. Leave **Preview** on. The app changes as you type, so you see each change at once.
6. Look under the editor. **No CSS problems found.** means the CSS is fine. Otherwise each problem shows with its line number, such as a missing `;` or `}`.
7. Click **Save**. Your new theme turns on, and Marinara asks **Keep this theme?** Click **Keep theme** within 15 seconds, or it goes back to your old look.

# Weather in Your Theme

When a story has weather, Marinara draws it over the chat: rain, snow, fog, falling leaves, petals, stars, a sun or a moon. Your theme can give all of it its own look. You can recolour the rain, make snow fall as pixel squares, swap leaves for pictures you drew, or turn your backdrop grey when it rains.

This guide walks you through it step by step. You need a theme of your own first. If you don't have one yet, the [Theme Author Guide](theme-author-guide.md) shows you how to make one in a few minutes. The [Weather](theme-author-guide.md#weather) section there is the short reference version of this page.

## How the weather works

The weather comes from the story. In a Roleplay or Game chat, the **World State** agent keeps track of the weather and the time of day, such as "heavy rain" and "night". Marinara reads those words and picks what to draw: rain streaks for "rain", flakes for "snow", stars and a moon for "night", and so on.

The app always does the drawing itself. Your theme doesn't draw anything. It sets a few `--mari-weather-` tokens (named settings, like `--primary`), and the app reads them and draws the weather your way. This keeps themes safe: nothing in a theme can run code, and the user's own settings, such as reduced motion, always win.

### Indoors the weather stays outside

When the story is inside, such as an inn, a bedroom or a World Maps room, the app doesn't rain across the whole screen. It keeps only the colour of the weather and the lightning flash, and the room stays dry. The app works out "inside" from the World State location ("Tideglass Inn, Brinewatch") or the World Maps place type. When it can't tell, the weather draws as usual. With **Weather Versions of Backgrounds** on (see [Roleplay Backgrounds](../roleplay/backgrounds.md#weather-versions-of-backgrounds)), the background picture itself shows the rain on the windows, and the moving weather comes back, drawn only on the window glass. Your theme's weather look applies there too.

### The weather with no theme

This is a rainy night with no theme: thin pale streaks over a dark blue wash. The pictures further down show the same chat with three starter themes.

# Custom CSS Themes

A theme changes the whole look of Marinara: colors, fonts, pictures and the shape of panels. Marinara has a gallery of ready-made starter themes you can download. You can also import a theme someone shared, or make your own.

For a quick change with no theme at all, see [Appearance Settings](appearance-settings.md) or [Ready-made chat window styles](#ready-made-chat-window-styles). To make your own theme, the [Theme Author Guide](theme-author-guide.md) walks you through it step by step.

## What a custom theme is

A theme is a block of CSS, the code web pages use for colors, fonts and spacing, plus any pictures and fonts it brings along. Themes are saved on your Marinara server, so a theme you install shows up on every device that connects to it. Only one theme is on at a time, and you can keep as many as you like.

## Where to find themes

Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections. In the classic layout it is **Settings → Addons → Theme Library**.

The section has:

- **Create Theme** and **Import File** at the top.
- **Allow themes with HTML (I accept the risk)**, off by default. See [Themes with HTML](#themes-with-html).
- **Installed Themes**: **Default Theme**, then your own themes, then the starter themes you downloaded.
- **Browse the theme gallery**: the starter themes you can download.

## Starter themes

Starter themes aren't part of the install, so they take no space until you want one. They live in the theme gallery, and Marinara downloads a theme only when you pick it.

1. Click **Browse the theme gallery** under **Installed Themes**. Marinara needs an internet connection for this.
2. Each theme shows a preview, a short description, its size and its tags.
3. Click **Download** next to the ones you like. They appear under **Starter themes** in **Installed Themes**, ready to switch on.

## Your first theme, step by step

A theme is a short list of settings written in CSS, the language web pages use for colours and fonts. You don't need to know CSS to start. Each line looks like `--name: value;`: a **token** (a named setting that starts with `--`), a colon, the value, and a semicolon.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections.
2. To change a starter theme, download one you like from **Browse the theme gallery**, find it under **Starter themes** and click **Clone + Edit** (the copy icon). Marinara makes your own copy, named for example "Petal OS (my copy)", and opens it in the editor. Starter themes stay read-only, so the original is always there. To start from scratch instead, click **Create Theme**. Its template has lines between `/*` and `*/`, which are switched off. Delete those marks around a line to switch it on.
3. Type a name in the name box.
4. Change a colour. Find a line such as `--primary: #3fae7a;` and replace the colour. `#3fae7a` is a hex colour code. Any colour picker on the web gives you one. Names such as `teal` work too.
5. Leave **Preview** on. The app changes as you type, so you see each change at once.
6. Look under the editor. **No CSS problems found.** means the CSS is fine. Otherwise each problem shows with its line number, such as a missing `;` or `}`.
7. Click **Save**. Your new theme turns on, and Marinara asks **Keep this theme?** Click **Keep theme** within 15 seconds, or it goes back to your old look.
